description: D4(b) step 1 of 5 — ASSESS, and gate the rest of the program on measured evidence (docs/DECISION-D4-CLDF-AND-WIKIBASE.md §5). The decision is taken: Wikibase becomes the canonical store because it natively models statements + qualifiers + references + ranks, so 'true at time T, place P, per source S' is a PRIMITIVE rather than a TSV convention that every reader has to reconstruct — and there are proven digital-humanities deployments to learn from (FactGrid, Enslaved.org, Rhizome ArtBase, plus a peer-reviewed CIDOC-CRM-over-Wikibase modelling method). What is NOT decided is whether pinakes can carry the operational load, and that is what this tasklist measures rather than assumes. The honest costs, stated up front so they are designed for rather than discovered: a FOUR-SERVICE stack (MediaWiki + a relational backing store + a triplestore query service + the updater), which the Wikibase project's own guidance says may demand dedicated sysadmin attention; an INHERITED MIGRATION — the Blazegraph-based query service is end-of-life, the WDQS graph split went live 2025-05-09 and the legacy endpoint sunset in Dec 2025, so a new deployment lands on QLever-era tooling rather than the documentation most tutorials assume; and a realistic 2-3 MONTH program across the five tasklists 120-124, not a sprint. A DOCUMENTED FALLBACK exists and is a legitimate outcome of this tasklist, not a failure: Oxigraph (Apache-2.0, single binary, no updater, no MediaWiki) with the Wikibase DATA MODEL replicated on top — pinakes gets statements/qualifiers/references/ranks and loses the curation UI and the ecosystem tooling. This tasklist stands the stack up for real, measures it, and writes the go / fallback decision down with the numbers attached. Scope: infra (a local/dev deployment under infra/), a measured evaluation, and the decision record. No corpus change, no schema change.

userStories.title: Stand the four-service stack up reproducibly and measure it
userStories.description: Deploy a real Wikibase stack (MediaWiki + backing DB + query service + updater) as reproducible infrastructure under infra/, on current, non-end-of-life query-service tooling, and record what it actually costs to run.
acceptanceCriteria: A reproducible deployment lives under infra/ (compose or equivalent, pinned image digests/versions, no `latest`) and a documented single command brings all four services up from a cold checkout to a state where an item can be created and read back through both the MediaWiki API and the SPARQL endpoint — verified end to end, not asserted.

The query-service leg is explicitly resolved: which engine is deployed, whether it is the Blazegraph-era service or QLever-era tooling, what the updater pipeline is, and what the upgrade path is given the legacy WDQS endpoint's Dec-2025 sunset — with the versions and the evidence links recorded, so this is never re-litigated from memory.

Measured operating numbers are recorded: cold-start time, steady-state memory and disk footprint per service, the observed lag from a write through the updater to SPARQL visibility, and what happens to each of those when the updater is stopped and restarted with a backlog.

userStories.title: Load a representative corpus slice and measure import + query at scale
userStories.description: A stack that works on one item proves nothing. Load a representative slice of the real corpus and measure whether import throughput and query latency support the atlas's actual access patterns.
acceptanceCriteria: A representative slice of the current corpus (at minimum: languages + families with their genealogy edges, and one cross-domain lineage slice) is loaded into the stack, with the loader recording items/statements per second and total wall-clock — extrapolated honestly to full-corpus scale including the post-113 ingested substrate.

The atlas's real read patterns are benchmarked against SPARQL and compared against the current Neo4j/DuckDB timings for the same questions: an ancestry traversal, a temporal-and-geographic filter, and a cross-domain lineage join — with the numbers tabulated, including the cases where the current stack wins.

The statement/qualifier/reference/rank model is exercised on a real case that the TSV schema handles badly today — one fact that is true at time T, in place P, per source S, with a competing claim from a second source at a different rank — proving the modelling benefit concretely rather than in the abstract.

userStories.title: Write the go / fallback decision down, with the numbers attached
userStories.description: Convert the measurements into a recorded decision: proceed with Wikibase as canonical, or take the documented Oxigraph fallback. Either outcome closes this tasklist; an unrecorded outcome does not.
acceptanceCriteria: A decision record in docs/ states the outcome — Wikibase-canonical or the Oxigraph fallback — with the US-1/US-2 numbers as its evidence, an explicit statement of the ops burden being accepted (who runs the four services, and what the failure modes are), and the criteria that would reverse it.

If the outcome is the fallback, the record specifies exactly what 'replicate the Wikibase data model on Oxigraph' means for pinakes — how statements, qualifiers, references and ranks are represented, what is lost (the curation UI, the Wikibase ecosystem tooling, the MediaWiki edit history), and which of 121-124 change shape as a result — so the remaining program stays runnable either way.
docs/DECISION-D4-CLDF-AND-WIKIBASE.md §5 is updated to point at the outcome, and the ROADMAP Phase-D rows reflect it; `.chief/verify.sh` passes.
